channel.title: elect.ng News
channel.description: Nigeria election news, history and analysis from the elect.ng Editorial Desk.

item.title: Darius Ishaku ₦27bn trial: witness says ex-governor never gave him instructions
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: A cashier testifying for the EFCC in the trial of the former Taraba governor told an Abuja court that payment instructions came from Ishaku's co-defendant, a former permanent secretary, and other officials.

item.title: "Good riddance": NDC accuses APC of buying its candidates as defections mount
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: After its Bauchi governorship candidate resigned, the Nigeria Democratic Congress said the APC was luring its candidates with money and appointments and promised to replace anyone who leaves.

item.title: NDC moves Obi–Kwankwaso campaign council launch to 26 October
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress postponed the inauguration of its presidential campaign council from 20 to 26 October because Peter Obi had an important engagement abroad.

item.title: Wike tells PDP members in Abuja to back Tinubu; Turaki-led PDP says no
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: The FCT minister, who coordinates the APC presidential campaign in the capital, promised logistics to PDP members who campaign for Tinubu. The PDP's interim leadership said true party members will not support the ruling party.

item.title: "You are the Egypt Nigerians want to escape": Atiku answers Tinubu's Moses remark on subsidy
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: President Tinubu likened calls to restore the petrol subsidy to asking Moses to lead the Israelites back to Egypt. Atiku Abubakar turned the comparison against him and repeated his plan for limited support for locally refined fuel.

item.title: Tinubu opens his 2027 campaign in Kaduna on Saturday
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: The APC presidential campaign flags off in Kaduna State on 24 October, with Port Harcourt and Maiduguri next, campaign director-general Abdulaziz Yari has said.

item.title: Kwankwaso at 70: Tinubu says party lines won't end their friendship
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: President Tinubu, NDC presidential candidate Peter Obi and Kano Governor Abba Yusuf paid tribute to Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, now Obi's running mate, as he turned 70 on 21 October.

item.title: G100 coalition: seven weeks on, still no common opposition candidate for 2027
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Six opposition parties agreed at an August summit to draft five unity documents and a route to a single presidential candidate. Their coordinator says progress has been made, but the ADC and NDC are openly at odds.

item.title: Baba-Ahmed: Tinubu has failed on the economy and security
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: The PRP national chairman, a former adviser to Vice-President Kashim Shettima, told Channels Television that Nigerians have yet to feel the benefits of the government's policies and that insecurity could keep northern voters at home.

item.title: NLNG dividends row: Makinde says states are owed ₦250bn each; Presidency says the sums don't add up
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: The Oyo governor and APM presidential candidate accused the federal government of holding back NLNG dividends due to the states. Bayo Onanuga replied that the claim would require more than $25 billion in a single payout.

item.title: Rivers peace deal: Assembly reinstates three pro-Fubara lawmakers after Wike visit
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: A day after Nyesom Wike led Assembly members and all 23 council chairmen to Governor Siminalayi Fubara's home, the Amaewhule-led House reversed the 2024 decision that declared three Fubara loyalists' seats vacant.

item.title: Police fire teargas at #EndSARS memorial at Lekki Toll Gate on sixth anniversary
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Mourners who gathered to lay wreaths for victims of the October 2020 shooting were dispersed before the ceremony began. Lagos governorship candidates Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour and Funso Doherty were among those caught in the teargas.

item.title: "Tell them no": Peter Obi clarifies remarks to UK Nigerians on sending money home
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: At a town hall in the UK, the NDC presidential candidate told Nigerians abroad to stop sending money to relatives and to push for better leaders instead. After a video spread, he said his opponents had twisted his message.

item.title: APC campaign denies plot against Atiku after Timi Frank's letter to Trump
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Former APC spokesman Timi Frank, now in the ADC, asked US President Donald Trump and other leaders to intervene over alleged threats to Atiku Abubakar. The Tinubu campaign called the claim baseless and dared him to give evidence to security agencies.

item.title: 2027 voter register: INEC missed the online publication deadline, and Atiku wants answers
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: The Electoral Act 2026 required INEC to publish the preliminary register online at least 90 days before the 16 January election. That deadline passed on 18 October with nothing online, and the ADC candidate has demanded the full list by ward.

item.title: Patrick Dele Cole, ex-ambassador and Daily Times chief, dies in London at 86
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: The journalist-diplomat, who ran the Daily Times, represented Nigeria in Brazil and Argentina and advised President Obasanjo on international relations, died after weeks of ill health.

item.title: Reuben Fasoranti, Afenifere leader and NADECO veteran, dies at 100
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: The educationist who served in Adekunle Ajasin's cabinet, led the Yoruba group Afenifere and opposed military rule has died months after his centenary. Ondo State Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa announced his death.

item.title: Emmanuel Uduaghan, former Delta governor, dies at 71
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: The medical doctor who governed Delta State from 2007 to 2015 died on 19 October 2026, three days before his 72nd birthday. President Tinubu and Governor Sheriff Oborevwori led the tributes.

item.title: Ebola: Senate orders entry screening, moves to replace 1926 Quarantine Act
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Senators voted for compulsory health checks at airports, seaports and land borders and asked for emergency funds, but Senate President Godswill Akpabio talked them out of visiting the entry points themselves.

item.title: Ebola in Abuja: Atiku demands audit of ₦10bn fund as Senate calls for emergency cash
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Atiku Abubakar wants a public account of ₦10 billion meant for Ebola preparedness, a day after Nigeria confirmed its first case since 2014. The Senate also told the government to release emergency money.

item.title: Governorship elections in Nigeria since 1999: results and history for all 36 states
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Every state's governorship history in one place: who has governed since 1999, which states vote off-cycle, how a governor is elected, and where the 2027 races stand after the wave of defections to the APC.

item.title: Anambra governorship elections since 1999: godfathers, court-made governors and APGA's long reign
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Anambra has had a governor installed by the Court of Appeal, Nigeria's first female governor, a governor removed by the Supreme Court after 17 days, and two decades of APGA rule. Every governorship result since 1999.

item.title: Imo governorship elections since 1999: the Supreme Court judgment that made a fourth-place candidate governor
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Imo has voted out a sitting governor, elected an APGA governor, and in January 2020 saw the Supreme Court remove Emeka Ihedioha and install Hope Uzodimma, who had finished fourth. Every governorship result since 1999.

item.title: Enugu governorship elections since 1999: PDP landslides, a 3,343-vote finish and Mbah's move to the APC
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Enugu gave the PDP some of its biggest wins anywhere for 20 years, then nearly lost to the Labour Party in 2023. In 2025 Governor Peter Mbah took the state into the APC. Every governorship result since 1999.

item.title: Ebonyi governorship elections since 1999: from Egwu and Elechi to Umahi's APC switch
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Ebonyi elected PDP governors for 20 years, often with lopsided margins, until Governor Dave Umahi crossed to the APC in 2020 and handed over to his Speaker. Every governorship result since 1999, and the 2027 race.

item.title: Abia governorship elections since 1999: from Orji Kalu's PPA to Alex Otti's Labour Party win
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Abia has had five governors since 1999 and has never voted out a sitting governor, but its 2015 result was overturned and restored in the courts, and in 2023 the Labour Party ended the PDP's long hold. Every result since 1999.

item.title: Edo governorship elections since 1999: Oshiomhole's court victory, Obaseki's switch and Okpebholo's win
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Edo voted off-cycle after a court installed Adams Oshiomhole in 2008. Since then a sitting governor has been denied his party's ticket, won anyway on another, and the APC has taken the state back. Every result since 1999.

item.title: Delta governorship elections since 1999: Ibori's dynasty, Ogboru's challenges and the move to the APC
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: The PDP won every Delta governorship election from 1999 to 2023, though one was annulled and the opposition came within 92,000 votes in 2011. In April 2025 the governor and his predecessor took the state into the APC.

item.title: Cross River governorship elections since 1999: PDP dominance, a rerun and the APC takeover
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Cross River elected PDP governors for 24 years, often with huge margins, then followed Governor Ben Ayade into the APC. Every governorship result since 1999, including the 2008 rerun, and the 2027 race.

item.title: Bayelsa governorship elections since 1999: from Alamieyeseigha and Jonathan to a Supreme Court reversal
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Bayelsa produced a President, lost a governor to a money-laundering scandal, had a 2007 result annulled, and in 2020 saw the Supreme Court remove its governor-elect a day before his swearing-in. Every result since 1999.

item.title: Akwa Ibom governorship elections since 1999: PDP landslides, then a governor crosses to the APC
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: The PDP won every Akwa Ibom governorship election from 1999 to 2023, several with more than a million votes. In 2025 Governor Umo Eno took the state into the APC. Every result since 1999 and the 2027 field.

item.title: Ekiti governorship elections since 1999: impeachment, emergency rule and the state that kept changing governors
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Ekiti voted out three sitting governors, had one impeached and another removed by the Court of Appeal, and lived under emergency rule. In 2026 Biodun Oyebanji became the first to win a second term in a row.

item.title: Ondo governorship elections since 1999: Mimiko's court victory, Akeredolu's death and Aiyedatiwa's landslide
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Ondo has voted out a sitting governor, seen a court hand the governorship to the runner-up, elected a Labour Party governor twice and, after Rotimi Akeredolu's death in office, given his deputy a 72% landslide.

item.title: Osun governorship elections since 1999: a court-made governor, a 482-vote rerun and Adeleke's comeback
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Osun has had a governor installed by the Court of Appeal three years into a term, a 2018 result reversed by a rerun, a 2022 winner removed and restored by the courts, and in 2026 a re-election on a third party's ticket.

item.title: Oyo governorship elections since 1999: impeachment, a broken "jinx" and Makinde's two landslides
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Oyo voted out two sitting governors, saw one impeached and restored by the courts, and gave Abiola Ajimobi the first second term in its history. Seyi Makinde has since won twice by wide margins. Every result since 1999.

item.title: Ogun governorship elections since 1999: from Osoba to Abiodun and a 13,915-vote finish
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Ogun has voted out a sitting governor, swung between the AD, PDP, ACN and APC, and in 2023 re-elected Dapo Abiodun by fewer than 14,000 votes. The results since 1999 and the 2027 field.

item.title: Plateau governorship elections since 1999: emergency rule, impeachment and two close finishes
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Plateau has had a governor suspended under emergency rule, an impeachment the Supreme Court overturned, an APC breakthrough in 2015 and a 2023 winner removed and then restored by the courts. Every result since 1999.

item.title: Niger State governorship elections since 1999: from the PDP to the APC and Umaru Bago
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Home state of two former military rulers, Niger was a PDP state until 2015, when the son of one general beat the son of another. Every governorship result since 1999 and the 2027 race.

item.title: Nasarawa governorship elections since 1999: a 4,425-vote upset and a governor saved by the Supreme Court
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Nasarawa elected Nigeria's only CPC governor in 2011 by fewer than 5,000 votes, and in 2023 a tribunal briefly removed its governor before the higher courts restored him. Every result since 1999.

item.title: Kwara governorship elections since 1999: the Saraki dynasty and "O to ge"
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: For two decades the Saraki family decided who governed Kwara. In 2019 the "O to ge" ("Enough is enough") campaign ended that, and AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq won every local government. Every result since 1999, and the 2027 race.

item.title: Kogi governorship elections since 1999: a rerun, a candidate who died mid-count and the Bello years
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Kogi votes off-cycle because of a 2008 rerun. Its 2015 election was thrown into confusion when the leading candidate died before the result was declared, and a substitute became governor. Every result since 1999.

item.title: Benue governorship elections since 1999: Akume, Suswam, Ortom and a priest in Government House
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Benue was a PDP state for 16 years, elected a governor who switched parties twice, and in 2023 chose a suspended Catholic priest. The results since 1999, and a 2027 race against a former Attorney-General.

item.title: Zamfara governorship elections since 1999: sharia, a Supreme Court shock and two defeated incumbents
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Zamfara introduced sharia criminal law, saw the Supreme Court hand every 2019 seat to the party that came second, and has voted out two sitting governors. In 2027 Governor Dauda Lawal runs on the APC ticket.

item.title: Sokoto governorship elections since 1999: Wamakko, Tambuwal and a 342-vote result
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Sokoto has seen an annulled election, a governorship cut short by the Supreme Court, a Speaker who became governor and switched parties, and in 2019 one of the narrowest wins in Nigerian history.

item.title: Kebbi governorship elections since 1999: a rerun ordered by the Supreme Court and a teachers' leader in power
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Kebbi has had four governors since 1999. One won his second term only after the Supreme Court annulled the first result; the current governor was national president of the teachers' union. In 2027 he faces a former Attorney-General.

item.title: Katsina governorship elections since 1999: the state that produced two presidents
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Umaru Musa Yar'Adua governed Katsina before becoming President, and Muhammadu Buhari's home state swung to the APC with him in 2015. Every governorship result since 1999, and the 2027 race.

item.title: Kaduna governorship elections since 1999: from Makarfi to Uba Sani's 10,806-vote win
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Kaduna has had six governors since 1999: one became Vice-President, one died in a helicopter crash and one lost his seat to Nasir El-Rufai. Its 2023 race was decided by less than one percentage point.

item.title: Jigawa governorship elections since 1999: Turaki, Lamido, Badaru and Namadi
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Jigawa has changed ruling party twice since 1999, each time with the national tide. In 2027 Governor Umar Namadi faces the son of former governor Sule Lamido for the second time.

item.title: Yobe governorship elections since 1999: the state the PDP never won
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Yobe has elected an opposition or APC governor at every election since 1999, through a governor's death in office and the Boko Haram insurgency. The results, the margins and the 2027 field.

item.title: Taraba governorship elections since 1999: a PDP stronghold until 2026
item.dc:creator: elect.ng Editorial Desk
item.description: Taraba elected a PDP governor at every election from 1999 to 2023, through a plane crash that left the state without an active governor, a tribunal ruling that briefly handed victory to "Mama Taraba", and a governor's jailing. Then the governor joined the APC.
